80025.subject: Base Writes a Seize Function Into Its Token Standard
80025.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* **[Base](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/base-ships-cobalt-with-conditional-transactions-and-a-seize-function)**[ shipped Cobalt with condition-bound transactions and a seizeWithMemo function on its B20 token standard](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/base-ships-cobalt-with-conditional-transactions-and-a-seize-function)

* **[ESMA](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/esma-proposes-mica-rules-for-defi-gateways-staking-and-lending)**[ proposed licensing the front ends that route EU users into DeFi, plus staking and lending duties](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/esma-proposes-mica-rules-for-defi-gateways-staking-and-lending)

* **[Abracadabra](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/abracadabra-proposes-winding-down-mim-at-four-cents-on-the-dollar)**[ proposed winding down MIM at about four cents against $21 million of bad debt](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/abracadabra-proposes-winding-down-mim-at-four-cents-on-the-dollar)

* **[Open USD](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/open-usd-launches-as-stripe-s-default-stablecoin)**[ went live as Stripe's default stablecoin, with Coinbase access due Oct. 1](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/open-usd-launches-as-stripe-s-default-stablecoin)

* **[Lighter's LIT](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/lighter-token-drops-after-robinhood-perps-plan)**[ fell 13% after Robinhood routed its US perps through Bitstamp and its own FCM](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/lighter-token-drops-after-robinhood-perps-plan)

Five weeks ago Coinbase put seven US stocks onchain as B20 tokens on Base. On Wednesday Base shipped the function that lets whoever holds the right role take those tokens out of a wallet, move them to an address the issuer has authorized, and attach a note explaining why.

Base [activated Cobalt on mainnet](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/base-ships-cobalt-with-conditional-transactions-and-a-seize-function), the year's third upgrade, and the release adds seizeWithMemo to the shared B20 surface. The caller needs the SEIZE_ROLE, the source wallet has to be blocked under the token's policy, and the destination has to be approved. Hours earlier ESMA [asked the European Commission to license the front ends](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/esma-proposes-mica-rules-for-defi-gateways-staking-and-lending) that route EU users into DeFi.

Coinbase's tokenized equities arrived with [transfer restrictions in the contracts](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/coinbase-launches-tokenized-stocks-on-base) in August, and the rest of DeFi wired itself to them anyway. Morpho [opened borrowing against them](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/morpho-coinbase-tokenized-stocks-borrowing-base) in September, Aave [took seven of them as collateral on Base](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/aave-adds-coinbase-stock-tokens-as-collateral-on-base) last week, and holder counts [passed 4.3 million across chains](https://thedefiant.io

Caption: 

# Book review: A Fabulous Debt

The craze for fixed-income investing hit such a fever pitch in 1820s London that investors were clamoring to purchase debt from high-risk borrowers like the newly independent Latin American nations of Chile and Peru. Even the country of Poyais was able to borrow at a mere 6%.

Unfortunately for London’s investors, Poyais did not exist. It was a “humongous, comically elaborate lie," financial journalist Robin Wigglesworth says.

The lie was told by the improbably named Gregor MacGregor, a soldier of fortune turned financial fraudster who convinced investors that an empty patch of Central American jungle he had received in return for his mercenary services was a fully fledged nation, complete with a bustling capital city, gold-filled rivers, fertile farmland, and an elaborate system of laws and government.

It was just plausible enough to be believed, apparently, because the fictional nation of Poyais was able to borrow the staggering sum of £200,000 from the City of London — a colorful example of the madness that bond investors periodically succumb to.

In “[A Fabulous Debt: The Epic Story of How Bonds Built the Modern World](https://www.amazon.com/Fabulous-Debt-Story-Bonds-Modern-ebook/dp/B0GGHN615Z/ref=sr_1_1?adgrpid=183606418702&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.sbKWztIldOLeejE5SSQ5cKftd9BpXBt9wyzAjohj3QTkwswb4GwKqT8iOuZo11XE4fbhSOiObWNxI5QZml4VBZiVn6s0R0tHP5klRWKVt7c.7NhSaOFkyiOSgzmqHTinwtEs2FOxPe7kC7bQs-ndtM8&dib_tag=se&hvadid=779537543880&hvdev=c&hvexpln=0&hvlocphy=9009671&hvnetw=g&hvocijid=8076117075117440842--&hvqmt=e&hvrand=8076117075117440842&hvtargid=kwd-2497969876969&hydadcr=21906_13654360_8544&keywords=wigglesworth+fabulous+debt&mcid=3644ef3888013d3bb886c57ce3a4889d&qid=1790775231&sr=8-1)”, Wigglesworth relates the history of bonds through a series of these kinds of mini-biographies — a “life and times” approach that makes a potentially dull topic anything but.
